name: Differentiable Volumetric Rendering (DVR)
aliases: Differentiable Volumetric Rendering (DVR) / Implicit Surface Differentiation
Differentiable Volumetric Rendering (DVR) / Implicit Surface Rendering
Implicit Surface Gradient via Implicit Differentiation
definition: A method to predict pixel color by casting a ray from camera origin r0 through pixel u, finding the first intersection p̂ with an isosurface defined by fθ(p) = τ, and returning the texture value tθ(p̂). It solves the problem of rendering implicit neural representations with differentiable gradients for optimization.
summary: Differentiable Volumetric Rendering trains implicit neural 3D representations from 2D images without 3D ground truth, avoiding voxel memory costs by representing geometry as a continuous neural isosurface.
